title: India and Seychelles Convene High-Level Bilateral Meeting to Strengthen Strategic Cooperation in Fisheries, Aquaculture, and the Blue Economy
body_text:
The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India, hosted a high-level bilateral meeting  on 25 August with a distinguished delegation from the Republic of Seychelles. The Seychelles delegation was led by H.E. Mr. Wallace Cosgrow, Minister of Fisheries, Agriculture and Blue Economy, while the Indian delegation was led by Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries. The meeting brought together senior officials and institutional representatives from both the nations to review existing frameworks, explore fresh avenues of mutual interest, and establish a robust collaborative road map for sustainable marine resource utilization.
Welcoming the Seychelles delegation, the Indian leadership underscored the deep-rooted maritime partnership between the two nations, reiterating India’s steadfast commitment to expanding technical cooperation in fisheries, aquaculture, advanced scientific research, and capacity-building. Both sides noted that their close alignment remains vital for advancing socio-economic stability, food and nutritional security across the Indian Ocean Region.
During the discussions, both delegations recognized the fisheries sector and the broader blue economy as critical pillars for driving economic growth, generating rural employment, and fostering sustainable development. Highlighting India's landmark achievements, the Indian delegation shared that national fish production has reached an unprecedented 19.7 million tonnes, with seafood exports valued at USD 8.46 billion. India also detailed its ongoing initiatives in sustainable fisheries management, responsible harvesting practices, and technology-driven infrastructure development.
The comprehensive agenda covered diverse technical areas for potential joint development, including marine aquaculture (mariculture), modern hatchery establishment, tuna fisheries optimization, stock assessment, advanced post-harvest engineering, and comprehensive marine conservation. Both countries explored immediate opportunities for knowledge transfer through targeted technical studies, structured fisheries extension services, and formal institutional training programmes.
A significant focus was placed on accelerating innovation and digital transformation within the sector. The delegations explored concrete partnerships in fisheries data systems, monitoring, control, and surveillance (MCS) infrastructure, and the deployment of emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) in harvest management. Additional emphasis was laid on value chain development particularly for tuna processing, product diversification, and sustainable fish waste management. To ensure long-term, systemic progress, both sides agreed on the necessity of a structured annual work plan, regulatory alignment, accelerated commercialization of joint scientific research, reciprocal laboratory access, and the collaborative design of impactful pilot projects.
The Seychelles delegation expressed keen interest in accelerating the implementation through a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) exclusively in the field of fisheries and aquaculture with an advanced work plan.  They emphasized the importance of setting up institutionalized engagement frameworks to facilitate seamless, continuous communication between administrative bodies, academic researchers, and technical experts from both nations.
Concluding the session, both sides underscored the value of mutual exposure visits, specialized technical exchanges, and the cross-leveraging of national Centres of Excellence to build institutional capacity and propagate international best practices. The high-level meeting concluded on a highly constructive and optimistic note, reaffirming a shared vision to translate diplomatic commitments into impactful, result-oriented action plans that secure long-term maritime prosperity for both India and Seychelles.

ministry.name: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

enrichment.summary: India's Department of Fisheries hosted a high-level bilateral meeting with Seychelles on 25 August, led by Secretary Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi and Seychelles' Minister H.E. Wallace Cosgrow, to strengthen cooperation in fisheries, aquaculture, and the blue economy. India shared that national fish production has reached 19.7 million tonnes with seafood exports worth USD 8.46 billion. The two sides discussed mariculture, tuna fisheries, hatchery development, AI-based harvest management, and monitoring/surveillance systems, with Seychelles proposing a dedicated bilateral MoU on fisheries and aquaculture.
enrichment.context: India and Seychelles share long-standing maritime ties rooted in Indian Ocean Region (IOR) security and economic cooperation, including defence and hydrographic partnerships. This meeting extends that relationship into the 'blue economy' domain, which has become a priority area for India as it seeks to project itself as a net security provider and development partner in the IOR under initiatives like SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region). Fisheries and aquaculture are significant components of India's blue economy policy, supported domestically by the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), which aims to boost fish production, exports, and rural livelihoods. The cited production and export figures reflect India's growing stature as one of the world's largest fish producers and exporters, particularly of shrimp. For Seychelles, a small island nation heavily dependent on tuna fisheries and marine tourism, technical collaboration with India on hatcheries, stock assessment, and value-chain development addresses both economic diversification and food security needs. The proposed MoU, if signed, would formalize technology transfer, capacity-building, and joint research, fitting into India's broader strategy of expanding technical and developmental partnerships across the Indian Ocean littoral states.

prelims_questions.question: India's Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) primarily aims to promote which sector?
prelims_questions.explanation: PMMSY is a flagship scheme of the Department of Fisheries aimed at sustainable development of the fisheries sector, boosting production, exports, and rural livelihoods, as referenced in the context of India's fisheries achievements.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Blue Economy' concept, discussed in India-Seychelles cooperation, primarily refers to:
options: Sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth while preserving marine ecosystem health
Trade agreements exclusively between island nations
Extraction of deep-sea minerals without regulation
Naval cooperation frameworks in the Indian Ocean
prelims_questions.explanation: The blue economy refers to sustainable, integrated use of ocean and marine resources for economic development, employment, and ecosystem preservation, as highlighted in the India-Seychelles discussions.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the 'Blue Economy' in India's foreign policy engagement with Indian Ocean littoral states, with reference to fisheries and aquaculture cooperation.
Examine the role of technology-driven interventions such as AI and digital monitoring systems in achieving sustainable fisheries management in India.

study_notes.reason: The release is essentially a diplomatic meeting readout; its enduring value lies in what it reveals about India's blue-economy diplomacy in the Indian Ocean Region rather than in any hard fact worth memorising, since the production/export figures are generic annual statistics repeated across many releases.

prelims.point: India's national fish production reported at 19.7 million tonnes, with seafood exports valued at USD 8.46 billion.
prelims.why_important: Aspirants should track India's ranking and output figures in fisheries as UPSC periodically tests sectoral statistics like this.

prelims.point: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is India's flagship umbrella scheme for fisheries sector development, underpinning achievements like those cited in this meeting.
prelims.why_important: PMMSY is a recurrently tested scheme name, and knowing it is the domestic engine behind India's fisheries diplomacy links prelims scheme knowledge to current affairs.

mains.point: India is using fisheries and blue-economy cooperation as a tool of strategic engagement with Indian Ocean littoral states, consistent with its SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) vision.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on India's maritime diplomacy or how economic/technical cooperation is deployed to advance strategic interests in the IOR.

mains.point: For small island states like Seychelles, technical collaboration on hatcheries, stock assessment and value-chain development addresses both economic diversification and food security constraints inherent to limited landmass and tuna-dependent economies.
mains.theme: Development partnership with small island states
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on India's role as a development partner to smaller neighbours, and on capacity-building as a form of soft power.

mains.point: Proposals such as AI-based harvest management and monitoring/surveillance systems reflect a broader shift toward technology-driven fisheries governance and sustainable resource management.
mains.analytical_use: Can be used in questions on application of emerging technologies (AI, digital monitoring) to natural resource governance and sustainability.

both.prelims_angle: Definition and scope of the blue economy concept, and its inclusion as a distinct sector in India's policy vocabulary alongside fisheries and aquaculture.
both.mains_angle: Its role as a pillar of India's economic growth strategy and regional diplomacy, linking sustainable ocean resource use to rural employment, food security and geopolitical positioning in the IOR.
